newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian preparations for 1997 grain harvest lag.
newsitem.headline: Russian preparations for 1997 grain harvest lag.

text.p: Russian farmers, coming out of a poor grain harvest and looking ahead to 1997, are behind schedule in sowing winter crops, Interfax news agency said on Tuesday.

The agency, quoting Ivan Gridasov, head of crops growing at the Agriculture Ministry, said farmers had sown 13.6 million hectares to winter crops for harvesting in 1997, or 1.5 million hectares less than at this time last year.
Sowing of winter crops in southern grain-belt areas takes place through the third week of November.
Over 36 million hectares of land had been ploughed for spring sowing, below the 41.5 million hectares ready at this time last year.
But Gridasov said only 18.5 percent of ploughed land had been treated with fertilisers and that low-quality seeds could again affect output.
Only 3.6 million tonnes of seeds out of 5.5 million checked for minimum quality levels, or less than 66 percent, were in proper condition. The level was identical to last year's.
Farmers had 8.7 million tonnes of seeds for spring sowing as of November, or about 89 percent of targeted levels.
Strategic buffer reserves of seeds were at a low 471,000 tonnes out of the needed 801,000 tonnes, and Gridasov said the ministry was taking measures to deliver supplies to needy areas.
The 1996 gross grain harvest is a poor 74.6 million tonnes, according to preliminary State Statistics Committee figures, and grain quality is low.
